reasoning: Google is currently on the Gemini 2.x series (latest: 2.5 Pro in March 2025). To release a model named Gemini 3.2 by May 2026 would require at least two major version increments (e.g., 3.0 → 3.1 → 3.2) in roughly 13 months. While the pace is fast, skipping multiple versions or naming a model 3.2 without preceding 3.0 is possible, it's historically unlikely. I estimate a 20% chance, far below the market’s 98.5% implied.
evidence_points: Gemini 2.5 Pro was released March 2025; no public roadmap mentions 3.0 or beyond.
Google’s previous cadence: Gemini 1.0 (Dec 2023), 1.5 (Feb 2024), 2.0 Flash (Dec 2024) — moving from 2.5 to 3.2 in 14 months would break that pattern.
The market description explicitly requires a Gemini 3.2 naming or direct 3.1 successor, not just any new model.
Even with acceleration, launching three distinct generation numbers (3.0, 3.1, 3.2) within a year is unprecedented for Google.
sources_consulted: Google DeepMind announcements and blog posts (2023-2025)
General knowledge of Gemini release history up to March 2025
